dossier.public_summary: The dip repeats every 1.24 days on the target star but its depth bounces from ~3300 to ~7300 ppm between orbits and between single transits, and the star itself pulses at exactly the same period with tens of thousands of ppm—typical of large starspots. The on-target flat-bottom transit shape is mimicked by spot-crossings, so the best explanation is stellar variability, not a 5.8 Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Star shows huge modulation at the dip period, ~0.56 of the dip depth (chi2 1311 dof 9), indicating spot / close-binary variability not a planet.
Measured rotation period 1.233 d matches signal period 1.23544 d in sectors 32,43,44,70,71 with amplitudes 59179 / 40524 / 45553 / 70787 / 80571 ppm, a perfect 1:1 coincidence not chance.

Depth changes dramatically between sectors (7364 to 3318 to 4888 to 5287 ppm, sector_depths_by_source changes_within_a_source verdict with SPOC 2-min p_constant 0.0 and TESS-SPOC p_constant 1.8002929135971535e-234, per-sector names: 32 7364±58, 43 3318±74,44 3562±30,70 4888±52,71 5287±51 ppm) inconsistent with a planet.
111 transits are highly inconsistent (chi2 5228.263556983027 dof 110, share_of_top_3 0.12 small but outliers at 11406±17.4σ, 18891±16.3σ, 10772±16.0σ ppm) as expected for evolving spot-crossings.
Machine scorer ranks far below median planet (0.5), consistent with variability / binary impostor.
